title: Pole order at a point of a product of integer powers of polynomials
statement:
Let $K$ be a field, $T$ an indeterminate, $K[T]$ the polynomial ring [def-weil-polynomial-ring], $K(T)$ the field of rational functions with its reduced presentations [def-weil-rational-function-field], $c\in K$, and let $m_c(P)$ be the multiplicity of $c$ as a root of $P\in K[T]$ [def-weil-root-multiplicity]. Then:

1. For nonzero $P,Q\in K[T]$: $m_c(P)=0$ if and only if $P(c)\neq0$; $m_c(PQ)=m_c(P)+m_c(Q)$; and $m_c\bigl(u\,(T-c)\bigr)=1$ for every $u\in K^\times$, in particular $m_c(1-c^{-1}T)=1$ when $c\neq0$.

2. Let $P_0,\ldots,P_n\in K[T]$ be nonzero, let $e_0,\ldots,e_n$ be integers, let $R=\prod_{j=0}^nP_j^{e_j}\in K(T)$, which is nonzero, let $R=N/D$ be its reduced presentation ($D$ monic, $\gcd(N,D)=1$), and put

$$
\nu=\sum_{j=0}^ne_j\,m_c(P_j)\in\mathbf Z.
$$

Then $m_c(N)-m_c(D)=\nu$, and at most one of $m_c(N)$, $m_c(D)$ is nonzero. Consequently, for an integer $m\geq1$, $R$ has a pole of order exactly $m$ at $T=c$ in the sense of [def-weil-rational-function-pole-order] if and only if $\nu=-m$, and $R$ is regular at $T=c$ if and only if $\nu\geq0$.

3. In particular, if for one index $j_0$ one has $e_{j_0}=-1$ and $m_c(P_{j_0})=1$, and $P_j(c)\neq0$ for every $j\neq j_0$, then $R=\prod_{j=0}^nP_j^{e_j}$ has a pole of order exactly $1$ at $T=c$.

source.place: ## Proof, second to fourth paragraphs: 'the order of vanishing of $P_i$ at $T=c^{-1}$ is the number of $r$ with $\alpha_{i,r}=c$' and 'As $P_0$ occurs with exponent $(-1)^{0+1}=-1$, $Z(X_0,T)$ has a pole of order exactly $1$ at $T=1$' (likewise for $P_{2d}$ and $T=q^{-d}$): the bookkeeping of root multiplicities in the product $\prod P_i^{(-1)^{i+1}}$ that these sentences take for granted; also literature/blueprint/master/blueprint/sec-zeta-weil/sk-thm-betti/_section.md, ## Proof: 'to read off the pole orders one must exclude cancellation against $N_\ell$ and further multiplicity from other factors of $D_\ell$'

proof.text: Step 1 (clause 1, vanishing and products). Let $P,Q\in K[T]$ be nonzero. By [lem-weil-root-multiplicity-pos-iff], $m_c(P)\geq1$ if and only if $P(c)=0$, i.e. $m_c(P)=0$ if and only if $P(c)\neq0$. By [lem-weil-root-multiplicity-mul], $m_c(PQ)=m_c(P)+m_c(Q)$.

source.place: ## Proof, second to fourth paragraphs (the bookkeeping is taken for granted there; the step is written by an agent)

proof.text: Step 2 (clause 1, linear factors). Let $u\in K^\times$. The constant polynomial $u$ is nonzero and its value at $c$ is $u\neq0$, so $m_c(u)=0$ by [lem-weil-root-multiplicity-pos-iff]. Next $m_c(T-c)=1$ by the definition [def-weil-root-multiplicity]: $(T-c)^1$ divides $T-c$, and $(T-c)^2$, of degree $2$, does not divide the nonzero polynomial $T-c$ of degree $1$, since a nonzero multiple of a polynomial of degree $2$ over a field has degree at least $2$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Hence by [lem-weil-root-multiplicity-mul] $m_c(u(T-c))=m_c(u)+m_c(T-c)=0+1=1$. When $c\neq0$, $1-c^{-1}T=(-c^{-1})(T-c)$ with $-c^{-1}\in K^\times$, so $m_c(1-c^{-1}T)=1$.

proof.text:
Step 3 (clause 2, a presentation by two polynomials). Let $J_+=\{j:e_j>0\}$, $J_-=\{j:e_j<0\}$ and put $A=\prod_{j\in J_+}P_j^{e_j}$, $B=\prod_{j\in J_-}P_j^{-e_j}$ in $K[T]$ (empty products are $1$). Since $K$ is a field, the leading coefficient of a product of nonzero polynomials is the product of their leading coefficients [def-weil-polynomial-ring], hence nonzero; so $A
eq0$ and $B
eq0$. In the field $K(T)$ [def-weil-rational-function-field], $P_j^{e_j}=1$ for $e_j=0$, so $R=\prod_jP_j^{e_j}=A/B$; in particular $R
eq0$ as a quotient of nonzero elements of a field.

source.place: ## Proof, second to fourth paragraphs (the bookkeeping is taken for granted there; the step is written by an agent)

proof.text: Step 4 (clause 2, multiplicities of $A$ and $B$). Applying Step 1 ($m_c(PQ)=m_c(P)+m_c(Q)$ for nonzero $P,Q$) repeatedly, by induction on the number of factors, gives $m_c(\prod_iQ_i)=\sum_im_c(Q_i)$ for finitely many nonzero $Q_i$, and in particular $m_c(Q^e)=e\,m_c(Q)$ for $e\geq0$ (with $m_c(1)=0$ from Step 2, $u=1$). Hence $m_c(A)=\sum_{j\in J_+}e_jm_c(P_j)$ and $m_c(B)=\sum_{j\in J_-}(-e_j)m_c(P_j)$, so $m_c(A)-m_c(B)=\sum_{j=0}^ne_jm_c(P_j)=\nu$ (the indices with $e_j=0$ contribute $0$).

Both sides are products of nonzero polynomials, so by [lem-weil-root-multiplicity-mul] $m_c(N)+m_c(B)=m_c(A)+m_c(D)$, i.e. $m_c(N)-m_c(D)=m_c(A)-m_c(B)=

proof.text: Step 6 (clause 2, no cancellation). Suppose $m_c(N)\geq1$ and $m_c(D)\geq1$. By the definition [def-weil-root-multiplicity], $T-c$ divides both $N$ and $D$. Since $\gcd(N,D)=1$, there are $U,V\in K[T]$ with $UN+VD=1$ [def-weil-coprime-polynomials], so $T-c$ divides $1$, i.e. $1=(T-c)W$ for some $W\in K[T]$; but $W\neq0$ and $\deg((T-c)W)=1+\deg W\geq1>0=\deg1$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring], a contradiction. Hence at most one of $m_c(N)$, $m_c(D)$ is nonzero.

proof.text:
Step 7 (clause 2, pole order and regularity). Let $m\geq1$. By [def-weil-rational-function-pole-order], $R$ has a pole of order exactly $m$ at $T=c$ if and only if $m_c(D)=m$. If $m_c(D)=m\geq1$, then $m_c(N)=0$ by Step 6, so $
u=-m$ by Step 5. Conversely if $
u=-m$, then $m_c(D)=m_c(N)+m\geq1$ by Step 5, so $m_c(N)=0$ by Step 6 and $m_c(D)=m$. For regularity: $R$ is regular at $c$ if and only if $D(c)
eq0$ [def-weil-rational-function-field], if and only if $m_c(D)=0$ by [lem-weil-root-multiplicity-pos-iff] ($D
eq0$). If $m_c(D)=0$ then $
u=m_c(N)\geq0$ by Step 5. If $m_c(D)\geq1$ then $m_c(N)=0$ by Step 6 and $
u=-m_c(D)<0$. So $R$ is regular at $c$ if and only if $
u\geq0$.

II §5). Mathlib has no statement of clauses 2-3 for RatFunc (searched; recorded). Proof in 8 steps: clause 1 from two new Mathlib leaves (lem-weil-root-multiplicity-mul = Polynomial.rootMultiplicity_mul, lem-weil-root-multiplicity-pos-iff = Polynomial.rootMultiplicity_pos) and the definition of m_c (m_c(T-c)=1 by degree); clause 2 by writing R=A/B with A, B the products of factors with positive and negative exponents, cross-multiplying N B = A D, additivity of m_c, and the coprimality of N and D (a common factor T-c would divide 1); pole order and regularity read off via def-weil-rational-function-pole-order; clause 3 as the case nu=-1. stmt_deps completed with def-weil-field, def-weil-coprime-polynomials (reduced presentation, gcd(N,D)=1) and def-weil-polynomial-root (P(c)). Statement unchanged.
